title: atomic-token-breakdown-scenarios-and-wires
summary: Working notes and quick wireframes for a compact 'atomic token breakdown' view that surfaces per-invocation cost and latency paths. Focused on scenario-driven flows, prioritization for next sprint, and a compact diff for canary rollouts.
background: Several prior explorations surfaced a need for both a slice-first UX and a single-invocation timeline. This doc experiments with a hybrid: an atomic row for each invocation that can expand into a time-rail (per-token waterfall) and a side-by-side cost attribution panel. Aim is to reduce time-to-investigate for customer incidents and to give non-engineering users an actionable explanation of cost drivers.
goals: Show per-invocation token timeline with cost attribution and KV-cache hits highlighted
Allow quick comparison between two invocations (canary vs baseline)
Provide actionable recommendations (batching, quantization, route change) inline
Keep UI performant for large traces (streamed render, progressive hydration)
wireframe_sketches: A: Compact list with atomic rows — each row shows: model badge, total tokens, total cost, p95 latency, expand chevron
B: Expanded row becomes a horizontal time-rail: tokens on x axis, colored segments for compute / io / cache / fallback, hover shows token-level cost and kernel used
C: Side panel that docks with attribution: token groups (prompt, system, kv, generation), with microledgers showing cumulative cost and per-token deltas
D: Diff mode — two rails stacked (canary above baseline) with token alignment heuristics and heatmap for divergence
E: Compact mobile-friendly mode that collapses the rail into an aggregated sparkline with tap-to-expand
screens: List view (default): 30 invocations, sortable by cost, latency, model, route
Invocation detail: rail + attribution + timeline events (cache miss, fallback, retry)
Compare view: selectable two invocations, alignment controls, token-diff legend
Recommendations drawer: suggested action, estimated delta (cost & latency), one-click apply to routing policy (requires perms)
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to quickly see which tokens caused a spike so I can check cache/prefix issues
As a PM, I want to compare a recent canary invocation to baseline to verify a quantization change reduced cost without adding latency
As an SE, I want one-click links to replay an invocation in the sandbox with identical context
As a support agent, I want an English summary of the top three cost contributors per invocation to paste into a customer response
acceptance_criteria: Expand/contract of an atomic row renders rail within 250ms for traces with <=1024 tokens
Diff mode aligns token boundaries with >90% correct heuristic on cases where prompts are near-identical
Recommendations drawer returns top-3 actions with estimated cost delta and confidence score
Feature respects RBAC: one-click policy apply only visible to users in 'platform-engineering' or 'admin' roles
open_questions: How do we represent partially cached KV entries (per-token or grouped)?
What's the canonical token grouping UX: fixed buckets (prompt/system/kv/gen) or dynamic clusters?
Do we need to surface kernel-level details (e.g., amx/flash-attn) in the default view or hide under an 'advanced' toggle?
Storage/retention: do we render historical rails from archived traces or only live-window traces?

design_decisions: Prefer progressive rendering to avoid TTI regressions on long traces
Keep default view aggregated to 1 row per invocation; expansion reveals token details
Use colorblind-safe palette and redundant patterning for token segment types
Hide kernel and quantization details behind an 'advanced details' disclosure to keep UX approachable
